title: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Long-horizon Work Agents
data_curation: Domain experts distill workflows into reusable Scene Blueprints b=(workflow, deliverable, required sources, domain decisions). An acquisition agent searches, reads, downloads and previews real-world resources (repositories, datasets, web sources) to fill each blueprint, keeping original file organization; each workspace is then profiled into a summary, workspace facts (factual anchors) and artifact schemas/statistics. The result, WorkForge-16K, has 16,665 tasks across 40 professional domains (top: Office Productivity 8.36%, Data & Database 8.21%), averaging 42.3 files, 279 KB and 21.9 rubrics per workspace over 60 file types (53% tabular). Real-world workspaces have 5.4x more files, 2.4x more file types and 13x larger footprint than LLM-synthesized matched ones. Trajectories are generated by GLM 5.3 under Claude Code and OpenClaw harnesses (avg 31.8 steps, 33.8 tool calls, 76,485 tokens).
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single SFT stage (no RL) on the scored trajectories, applied both to Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base and to the already post-trained Qwen3.5-27B; the paper instead studies data-volume scaling (non-nested 1K/3.6K/8K/16K subsets) and interaction-horizon scaling (1K-trajectory subsets of 0-20, 21-40, 41-60 turns), plus verifier-based trajectory selection (hybrid 0.5*S_sem + 0.5*S_prog >= 0.7 in the ablation).
method: A four-stage pipeline: workflow specification -> environment synthesis (one-to-many mapping of a blueprint to resource pools, then profiling) -> task generation -> trajectory generation. The task designer jointly produces a visible instruction and a hidden solution plan from blueprint + profile; key factual claims in the plan are verified against the workspace, and the verified facts define an atomic rubric set split into programmatic criteria (binary checks on artifacts/workspace state, averaged) and semantic criteria scored 0-10 by a criterion-configured LLM judge; both scores are kept separately. Task packages separate visible (workspace, instruction) from hidden (profile, plan, facts, rubrics, graders). SFT: full-parameter, verl SFT trainer with FSDP + Ulysses SP=4, AdamW (0.9, 0.95), peak LR 1e-5 cosine to 1e-7, 5% warmup, 5 epochs, global batch 64, 262,144-token max length, packing and per-assistant-message loss masks; 64 H20 GPUs (A3B) or 128 (27B).
eval_metrics: Five agent benchmarks: WildClawBench (Score, Pass@1, OpenClaw), Claw-Eval (Score, Pass^3 over 3 rollouts, OpenClaw), GDPval (official rubric score on 201 text-only of 220 tasks, Claude Code), APEX-Agents (Score, Pass@1, ReAct Toolbelt) and Agents' Last Exam (Score, Pass@1, Claude Code), decoded with vLLM at temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9, 32,768 tokens per response. WorkForge-A3B: WildClaw 29.9, ClawEval 53.3, GDPval 73.6, APEX 21.3, ALE 28.7/12.4 Pass@1. WorkForge-27B: 38.5, 65.4, 82.4, 29.9, 33.9. Ablations: hybrid verifier selection beats LLM-only and programmatic-only (ALE 22.11 vs 15.62 vs 14.89); ALE rises 15.7->28.7 from 1K to 16K trajectories.
key_results: SFT on WorkForge lifts Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base from 45.5 to 73.6 on GDPval and from 5.0 to 21.3 on APEX, beating the prior best sub-100B specialist ClawGym-30A3 on GDPval by 38.6 points. WorkForge-27B reaches 82.4 on GDPval, above Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (79.7) with roughly 15x fewer parameters.
evolution_note: WorkForge reacts to automated environment-synthesis work (EnvScaler, Agent World Model, ClawGym, NexForge) whose mock or LLM-synthesized workspaces are small and clean, arguing that real-world files and fact-anchored verifiers are needed for professional work agents. It pairs programmatic and rubric-based LLM judging in the style of PaperBench/Agent-as-a-judge, and its harness-transfer finding (Claude Code vs OpenClaw trajectories) points to harness alignment as a factor in agent post-training.
